key_caveat: The requester asks for a dashboard but their request require a causal analysis
caveats: A dashboard will only show correlation over time, not prove that the firmware sensitivity change caused the increase in cancellations. Confounding factors like seasonal activity shifts or user reporting behavior must be controlled. Additionally, Fall Alert Monitoring Dashboard already monitors daily cancellations by model, and raw telemetry in fall_alert_events does not support a truly 'live' stream, so building a second dashboard would duplicate BI assets and mislead leadership on causation.

key_caveat: 100K patients' audiograms raises privacy and de-identification questions
caveats: Pulling 100K patient records involves significant health data volume; verify data governance and privacy approval before sharing export files. Also, clarify sampling methodology: taking a purely random patient sample without stratification may bias toward active clinic users with repeated fitting sessions or non-standard test batteries.

caveats: A distribution alone will not prove whether clinician environment or patient need drives the setting. caveats: Users who opt into fall detection likely differ systematically (e.g., older, more tech-savvy, or different health profiles) from those who do not, making correlation easily mistakable for causation. Furthermore, our data catalog currently lacks explicit feature opt-in telemetry—we only log triggered events via fall_alert_events—so we must verify with mobile/firmware engineering how enablement can be reliably determined before building cohort models.

caveats: Pushing back on exporting a raw CSV of all app events over six months: this dataset would easily contain millions of rows, rendering spreadsheet exploration ineffective and risking privacy/compliance issues. Furthermore, correlation in drop-off does not equal causation—passive hearing aid wearers often do not need daily companion app interaction if their hearing settings are stable, so apparent churn might reflect satisfaction rather than disengagement. We need telemetry validation on app crashes before modeling churn reasons.
